title: Advancements in stress-testing methodologies for financial stability applications
summary: This ECB Occasional Paper provides a comprehensive overview of stress-testing methodologies developed by the ECB's Financial Stability Committee Working Group on Stress Testing (WGST) from 2018 to 2022. The paper details the development of 16 new models and 13 new datasets, covering credit risk, market risk, profitability, macroprudential analysis, and system-wide interconnectedness modeling. The WGST's work aimed to enhance EU-wide stress-testing exercises and broaden the use of stress-testing beyond risk assessment into policy evaluation and communication.
key_points: The WGST developed 16 new models, including 5 that replaced earlier models in the STAMP€ toolkit and 11 covering new areas not previously addressed by the ECB top-down toolkit
13 new datasets were integrated, including transaction-level data, to support enhanced stress-testing analysis
The top-down models cover credit risk (using both IFRS 9 and regulatory parameters), market risk, and profitability to assess default probabilities, revaluation losses, and income sources
Macro-micro models examine interactions between macroprudential policies, monetary policy changes, and financial stability outcomes
The Interconnected System-wide stress test Analytics (ISA) model captures interconnectedness among banks and non-banking financial institutions to address financial contagion
Validation efforts combine ex ante and ex post elements, comparing model performance against banks' forecasts and back-testing against past exercises
Stress-testing applications have expanded beyond challenging bank bottom-up submissions to include fully top-down exercises such as scenario, vulnerability, and sensitivity analyses
why_it_matters: This methodological paper is foundational for understanding how European regulators assess bank solvency and systemic risk. The enhanced stress-testing frameworks described here directly inform how the ECB and EBA conduct EU-wide stress tests that affect bank capital requirements, dividend policies, and ultimately credit availability in the economy. Financial market participants monitoring banking sector health need to understand these methodologies.
market_structure_context: This paper describes the evolution of financial stability assessment infrastructure in Europe, including the development of top-down models (credit risk under IFRS 9 and regulatory parameters, market risk, profitability), macro-micro models for macroprudential policy interaction, and system-wide models (ISA) capturing bank and non-bank interconnectedness. Validation frameworks and model execution infrastructure improvements are also documented.
